subject: Workplace Skills
title: Reversible Versus Irreversible Decisions
description: A fast breakdown of Reversible Versus Irreversible Decisions for builders.

hook.text: Jeff Bezos splits decisions into one-way doors and two-way doors. One-way doors need caution. Two-way doors need speed.

buildup.text: Most business decisions are two-way doors: reversible, low-cost to undo. Yet teams agonize over them equally.

discovery.text: Treat reversible decisions fast. Move quickly with 70% information. For irreversible ones, slow down and deliberate.

twist.text: Speed on reversible decisions is a competitive advantage. Slow companies lose not to smarter ones, but to faster ones.

climax.text: Before any decision, ask: can we undo this easily? If yes, decide fast. If no, gather more data and involve others.

punchline.text: Two-way door? Decide fast. One-way? Slow down.

quiz.question: How should leaders treat reversible decisions differently from irreversible ones?
options: Apply the same deliberation process to all decisions
Move fast on reversible decisions and slow down for irreversible ones
Delegate reversible decisions and personally handle irreversible ones
